question: A computer can do \(10{,}000\) additions per second. How many additions can it do in one hour?
solution:
The computer's rate is given per second, so first express one hour in seconds. There are \(60\) minutes in an hour and \(60\) seconds in each minute, giving
\[60\cdot60=3600\text{ seconds}.\]
At \(10000\) additions each second, the total is
\[10000\cdot3600=36000000\text{ additions}.\]
This is \(36\) million additions, choice B.
